title: Heterogeneous output pivotal probability
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p_i\in(0,1)$ for each $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and choose an output sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$ and coordinate $i$. The heterogeneous output pivotal probability of $f$ at $b$ in coordinate $i$ is the probability, under the product distribution on sign vectors whose coordinate $j$ is biased according to $p_j$, that changing coordinate $i$ makes $f$ output $b$.
hypotheses_covered: Each coordinate bias $p_i$ lies strictly between $0$ and $1$
$f$ maps sign vectors of length $n$ to signs
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definitions of the product distribution or of output pivotality, so their precise conventions cannot be confirmed.
